records.subject: spec-guard-claude-code-cli-hook
evidence: command:PATH=$HOME/.local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin claude -p --resume <release session> --fork-session --output-format json 'Release host check. Reply with exactly: ok'

result:exit 0; the fork's injected phase text had the location line (`branch `main` · worktree `<this repository>``) but no context line: a forked session's transcript file is created only when its first message is written, after UserPromptSubmit runs, so the hook found no file and stayed quiet as designed
command:PATH=$HOME/.local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin claude -p --resume <that fork> --output-format json 'Second host check. Reply with exactly: ok'

result:exit 0; the injected phase text read from the session transcript contained `- Session context: about 245 k tokens in the last turn (over 200k); every turn re-reads it. At the next task boundary, record decisions in the spec and start a new session.` after the counts line, plus the location line under the heading
result:the installed session_context.py run directly on the same transcript afterwards also reported 244658 tokens
limit:the first turn of a new or freshly forked session has no transcript yet, so it never carries the context line; a new session is small, so this only matters for --fork-session of a long one
limit:the module boundary line was not observed on a real host in this release; it is covered by the phase-guard regression (MODULE_DONE / DONE cases)
host:python3 resolved to /usr/bin/python3 3.9.6; the two calls cost $1.66 and $1.73
